definition: The largest artery in the abdomen, supplying blood to the lower body; located in the retroperitoneum and prone to aneurysms or occlusion.
meaning: Main highway for blood to your lower body
breakDown: Key screening target for aneurysms (AAA screening)
clinicalUse: Screen for aneurysms (AAA) - life-threatening if ruptures

definition: An abnormal whooshing sound heard over the abdomen due to turbulent blood flow, often indicating arterial stenosis or aneurysm.
meaning: Abnormal "whooshing" sound in the belly indicating turbulent flow
clinicalUse: Helps detect arterial stenosis or aneurysm before imaging

definition: A Doppler measurement used in renal artery evaluation; values less than 3 m/s² suggest stenosis by indicating delayed systolic upstroke.
meaning: Measures how fast blood speeds up at the start of systole
breakDown: Acceleration Index = speed of the "upstroke" of the waveform

memoryTrick.title: Think: "How fast does blood hit the gas?" 🚗💨

definition: Time from onset of systole to peak velocity in Doppler waveforms; greater than 70 ms indicates proximal stenosis (e.g., tardus parvus pattern).
meaning: Time it takes to reach peak velocity from the start of systole
clinicalUse: Identifies proximal stenosis causing tardus parvus pattern

definition: Sudden reduction in blood flow to tissues, often due to emboli or thrombosis, leading to pain, pallor, and potential tissue death.
meaning: Sudden loss of blood supply causing tissue emergency
breakDown: Usually caused by clot (thrombus) or embolus

memoryTrick.title: Remember the 6 P's: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Poikilothermia 🆘

clinicalUse: Medical emergency - tissue death if not treated quickly

definition: Death of tubular cells in the kidney, the most common cause of immediate postoperative renal transplant failure, often due to ischemia.
meaning: Death of kidney tubule cells - most common early transplant complication
clinicalUse: Most common cause of immediate postop renal transplant failure

definition: An artifact in Doppler ultrasound where high velocities appear wrapped around the spectrum, mimicking reversed or low flow.
meaning: Artifact where fast flow looks reversed or wrapped around
breakDown: Happens when velocity exceeds Nyquist limit
High velocity appears as reversed flow

memoryTrick.title: Think: "Too fast to track" 🏃‍♂️💨
points: Fix: increase scale or use CW Doppler

clinicalUse: Don't mistake aliasing for reversed flow - adjust your settings!

waveformClue.abnormal: high velocity wraps to opposite side of baseline

definition: Transient monocular vision loss due to temporary ischemia in the retinal artery, often a hemispheric symptom of carotid disease.
meaning: Temporary blindness in one eye from lack of blood flow
breakDown: Classic sign of carotid artery disease
clinicalUse: Hemispheric symptom - indicates carotid disease, stroke risk

definition: A non-invasive test comparing ankle and brachial systolic pressures; normal range 0.9-1.3, lower values indicate peripheral arterial disease.
meaning: Ratio comparing ankle pressure to arm pressure
clinicalUse: First-line screening for peripheral arterial disease (PAD)

definition: A deep vein in the lower leg accompanying the anterior tibial artery; often paired and drains the anterior compartment.
meaning: Deep vein in front of lower leg
clinicalUse: Check for DVT in lower leg deep veins
